title: Luke Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Luke 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness
Jesus returning in the power of the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness
questions.explanation: This event occurs first in the chapter as stated in Luke 4:1.

questions.question: How long was Jesus tempted by the devil in the wilderness?
questions.correctAnswer: 40 days
questions.explanation: The text states that Jesus was tempted for forty days in Luke 4:2.

questions.question: What did the devil first suggest Jesus do to prove he was the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Turn stones into bread
questions.explanation: The devil suggested this in Luke 4:3, asking Jesus to command a stone to be made bread.

questions.question: What was Jesus' response to the devil's suggestion about turning stones into bread?
options: It is written, man shall not live by bread alone
questions.correctAnswer: It is written, man shall not live by bread alone
questions.explanation: Jesus answered by quoting scripture in Luke 4:4.

questions.question: What did the devil show Jesus when he took him up into a high mountain?
options: All the kingdoms of the world
questions.correctAnswer: All the kingdoms of the world
questions.explanation: The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms in a moment of time as stated in Luke 4:5.

questions.question: What did the devil promise to give Jesus if he would worship him?
questions.correctAnswer: Power and glory
questions.explanation: The devil claimed he could give Jesus all this power and glory in Luke 4:6.

questions.question: What was Jesus' response to the devil's demand to worship him?
options: I am the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: Get thee behind me, Satan
questions.explanation: Jesus firmly rebuked the devil in Luke 4:8.

questions.question: To where did the devil bring Jesus to tempt him next?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The devil brought Jesus to Jerusalem as mentioned in Luke 4:9.

questions.question: What did the devil challenge Jesus to do from the pinnacle of the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Jump down
questions.explanation: The devil asked Jesus to cast himself down from the pinnacle in Luke 4:9.

questions.question: What scripture did the devil quote to Jesus regarding angels?
options: He shall give his angels charge over thee
questions.correctAnswer: He shall give his angels charge over thee
questions.explanation: The devil quoted this scripture in Luke 4:10.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about tempting the Lord?
options: It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.correctAnswer: It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
questions.explanation: Jesus stated this in Luke 4:12.

questions.question: What happened after the devil ended all the temptation?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that the devil departed from him for a season in Luke 4:13.

questions.question: After being tempted, where did Jesus return to?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee as stated in Luke 4:14.

questions.question: Jesus returned to Jerusalem after the temptation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states that Jesus returned to Galilee, not Jerusalem, in Luke 4:14.

questions.question: Jesus taught only in the temple after returning from the wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text says Jesus taught in their synagogues, not just the temple, in Luke 4:15.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Jesus' custom in Nazareth on the Sabbath day?
options: He went into the synagogue to read
questions.correctAnswer: He went into the synagogue to read
questions.explanation: Luke 4:16 states that Jesus went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, as was his custom.

questions.question: What does Luke 4:18 promise will happen if someone is anointed to preach the gospel?
options: They will be accepted in their own country
questions.correctAnswer: They will heal the brokenhearted
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 describes the anointing of Jesus to preach the gospel and includes the promise of healing the brokenhearted.

questions.question: What did Jesus declare about the scripture he read in the synagogue?
questions.correctAnswer: It was fulfilled
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:21, Jesus said, 'This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears,' indicating the fulfillment of the prophecy he read.

questions.question: What does Luke 4:24 teach about a prophet's acceptance?
options: No prophet is accepted in his own country
A prophet is honored in his own country
A prophet must perform miracles to be accepted
questions.correctAnswer: No prophet is accepted in his own country
questions.explanation: Luke 4:24 states, 'Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country,' emphasizing how familiar surroundings often lead to disbelief.

questions.question: What did the people in the synagogue do when they heard Jesus' words?
questions.correctAnswer: They were filled with wrath
questions.explanation: Luke 4:28 indicates that the people were filled with wrath after hearing Jesus' message.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when Jesus read from the book of Esaias?
options: They wondered at his gracious words
questions.correctAnswer: They wondered at his gracious words
questions.explanation: Luke 4:22 states that the people bore witness and wondered at the gracious words that came from Jesus' mouth.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the proverb, 'Physician, heal thyself'?
questions.correctAnswer: He rejected it
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:23, Jesus anticipates that they would use this proverb, indicating a rejection of their challenge.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he mentioned widows in the days of Elias?
options: God's favor was only on the widows
questions.correctAnswer: Only one widow received help
questions.explanation: Luke 4:26 shows that despite many widows in Israel, Elias was only sent to one widow, highlighting God's selective outreach.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'to preach the acceptable year of the Lord' represent?
options: A time of grace and favor
questions.correctAnswer: A time of grace and favor
questions.explanation: Luke 4:19 refers to the acceptable year of the Lord as a time of grace, aligning with the prophetic message of hope.

questions.question: Why did Jesus mention Naaman the Syrian in his teaching?
options: To highlight Israel's lack of faith
questions.correctAnswer: To highlight Israel's lack of faith
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:27, Jesus points out that Naaman was cleansed while many lepers in Israel were not, illustrating the lack of faith in his own country.

questions.question: What can we learn from Jesus' experience in the synagogue about handling rejection?
options: Rejection is painful and should be avoided
Rejection can be a sign of failure
Rejection does not define one's mission
Rejection is a reason to stop speaking
questions.correctAnswer: Rejection does not define one's mission
questions.explanation: Jesus faced rejection in Luke 4:29-30 but continued on his mission, teaching that rejection is part of a greater purpose.

questions.question: What does Jesus' teaching in Luke 4 suggest about compassion for the marginalized?
options: It is limited to certain groups
questions.correctAnswer: It is crucial for ministry
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 emphasizes that Jesus was anointed to preach to the poor and heal the brokenhearted, highlighting the importance of compassion in ministry.

questions.question: Does Luke 4:30 indicate that Jesus was ultimately captured by the crowd?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 4:30 shows that Jesus passed through the crowd unharmed, indicating he was not captured.

questions.question: Is it true that all the people in the synagogue agreed with Jesus' teaching?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 4:28 shows that the people were filled with wrath against Jesus' words, indicating disagreement.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus was accepted and praised by everyone in Nazareth?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 4:24 illustrates that Jesus noted a prophet is not accepted in his own country, indicating a lack of praise.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Luke 4:31, to which city did Jesus come down and teach on the Sabbath days?
questions.correctAnswer: Capernaum
questions.explanation: Luke 4:31 explicitly states that Jesus came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught there on the sabbath days.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people to Jesus' teaching in Luke 4:32?
options: They were astonished at his doctrine
questions.correctAnswer: They were astonished at his doctrine
questions.explanation: Luke 4:32 says that the people were astonished at his doctrine because his word was with power.

questions.question: In Luke 4:34, what title does the unclean spirit acknowledge Jesus by?
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy One of God
questions.explanation: Luke 4:34 records the unclean spirit crying out, 'I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God,' acknowledging Jesus by this title.

questions.question: How did Jesus deal with the unclean spirit in the man in the synagogue, according to Luke 4:35?
options: He rebuked the spirit and commanded it to come out
questions.correctAnswer: He rebuked the spirit and commanded it to come out
questions.explanation: Luke 4:35 states that Jesus rebuked the spirit saying, 'Hold thy peace, and come out of him,' and the spirit came out without harming the man.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction after Jesus cast out the unclean spirit in Luke 4:36?
options: They were all amazed and spoke among themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They were all amazed and spoke among themselves
questions.explanation: Luke 4:36 reveals that all the people were amazed and discussed among themselves the authority and power with which Jesus commanded the unclean spirits.

questions.question: According to Luke 4:40, what method did Jesus use to heal the sick who were brought to Him at sunset?
options: He laid his hands on every one of them
He spoke a word from a distance
questions.correctAnswer: He laid his hands on every one of them
questions.explanation: Luke 4:40 clearly states that Jesus laid his hands on every sick person brought to Him and healed them.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐξορκίζω' (exorkizō) used in Luke 4:35 mean?
options: To rebuke or command with authority
questions.correctAnswer: To rebuke or command with authority
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'ἐξορκίζω' translated as 'rebuked' in Luke 4:35 means to command or adjure with authority, especially in the context of casting out spirits.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Luke 4:18–19 when Jesus reads from Isaiah, proclaiming his mission?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18–19 uses an inclusio literary device, framing Jesus' mission statement with a quotation from Isaiah that sets the thematic boundaries of the passage.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is directly quoted and fulfills the prophecy mentioned in Luke 4:18-19?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 61:1-2
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18-19 quotes Isaiah 61:1-2, fulfilling the prophecy about the anointed one preaching good news to the poor and setting captives free.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Jesus' teaching about no prophet being accepted in his own country as mentioned in Luke 4:24?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 13:57
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:57 echoes Luke 4:24 by noting that Jesus was not accepted in His hometown, highlighting the common theme of prophetic rejection.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum in Luke 4:31?
options: He was tempted in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: He was rejected at Nazareth
questions.explanation: Luke 4:30 describes Jesus passing through the crowd that tried to throw Him down a hill in Nazareth, immediately preceding His teaching in Capernaum in Luke 4:31.

questions.question: What typological significance does Jesus’ rebuke of the unclean spirit in Luke 4:35 have in the context of Old Testament deliverance narratives?
options: It symbolizes the Messianic authority over evil
It is a metaphor for exile
It reflects the Day of Atonement rituals
It foreshadows the destruction of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the Messianic authority over evil
questions.explanation: Jesus' authority to command unclean spirits in Luke 4:35 typologically symbolizes His fulfillment of Old Testament expectations of a Deliverer who has power over evil forces.

questions.question: How does the use of the phrase 'Holy One of God' in Luke 4:34 connect to Old Testament understanding of holiness?
options: It identifies Jesus with the divine presence
It refers to a high priestly title
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies Jesus with the divine presence
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:34, 'Holy One of God' reflects Old Testament usage where holiness signifies God's unique divine presence, thus identifying Jesus with God’s holiness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 4:43, Jesus said He must preach the kingdom of God only in Capernaum.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 4:43 states that Jesus said He must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, not only in Capernaum.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 4:40 indicates that Jesus healed the sick after sunset by laying hands on them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 4:40 explicitly states that when the sun was setting, all who had sick with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and He laid His hands on each and healed them.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 4:4 teach about human reliance and divine provision?
options: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God
Man is sustained only by physical nourishment
God provides only material blessings to His people
Faith is unnecessary for physical survival
questions.correctAnswer: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God
questions.explanation: Luke 4:4 records Jesus affirming that true life depends not merely on physical sustenance but on the living word of God, teaching the doctrine that spiritual nourishment is essential for human existence.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's kingdom and authority is taught in Luke 4:6?
options: The devil claims delegated authority over earthly kingdoms
God's kingdom is limited to Israel alone
Satan has ultimate authority over the world
Jesus must seize kingdoms by force
questions.correctAnswer: The devil claims delegated authority over earthly kingdoms
questions.explanation: Luke 4:6 shows the devil asserting that the kingdoms of the world have been delivered to him and he can give them to anyone he wishes, teaching the doctrine of partial and temporary satanic rule under God's sovereign permissiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning prophetic rejection is taught in Luke 4:24?
options: No prophet is accepted in his own country
Prophets always receive honor from their people
Jesus was universally accepted in Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: No prophet is accepted in his own country
questions.explanation: Luke 4:24 teaches the doctrine that prophets, including Jesus Himself, often face rejection from their own people, highlighting the principle that divine revelation is frequently resisted in familiar contexts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 4:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Luke 4:1 shows Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness, demonstrating God's sovereignty in directing the mission and testing of the Messiah.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Luke 4:18 regarding Jesus' mission?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 emphasizes the Spirit of the Lord anointing Jesus to preach good news to the poor, heal the brokenhearted, and set at liberty those that are bruised, highlighting God's attribute of mercy.

questions.question: How does Luke 4:14 prepare for the theme of the Spirit's empowerment in the book of Acts?
options: It shows Jesus beginning His ministry in the power of the Spirit
It emphasizes Jesus' physical strength over spiritual power
It denies the Spirit's role in Jesus' ministry
It focuses solely on Jesus' human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus beginning His ministry in the power of the Spirit
questions.explanation: Luke 4:14 teaches that Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit, prefiguring the Pentecost empowerment of the church in Acts, thus establishing the continuity of the Spirit's work in salvation history.

questions.question: How does Luke 4:28–29 connect to the wider biblical theme of prophetic rejection and persecution?
options: It depicts Jesus' rejection and attempted violence against Him, fulfilling the pattern of prophets being opposed
It shows universal acceptance of Jesus' message
It denies any opposition to Jesus’ ministry
It indicates that prophets always succeed in their hometowns
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts Jesus' rejection and attempted violence against Him, fulfilling the pattern of prophets being opposed
questions.explanation: Luke 4:28–29 narrates how the synagogue listeners were filled with wrath and tried to kill Jesus, demonstrating the biblical motif that prophets often suffer rejection and hostility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 4:8 and Luke 4:12 teach about worship and testing God?
options: Worship belongs only to God and testing Him is forbidden
Satan deserves worship as a co-ruler
God commands testing as proof of faith
Worship can be shared among heavenly beings
questions.correctAnswer: Worship belongs only to God and testing Him is forbidden
questions.explanation: Luke 4:8 commands exclusive worship of God, and Luke 4:12 forbids tempting God, together teaching the doctrine that worship is reserved for God alone and that believers must not put God to the test.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of Scripture in temptation is taught by Luke 4:4 and Luke 4:12?
options: Scripture is the authoritative defense against temptation
Scripture has no relevance in spiritual trials
Jesus ignored Scripture during His temptation
questions.correctAnswer: Scripture is the authoritative defense against temptation
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:4 and 4:12, Jesus counters the devil's temptations by citing Scripture, demonstrating the doctrine that God's word is the ultimate weapon against sin and temptation.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is found in Luke 4:18 and Luke 4:43 regarding Jesus' mission?
options: Jesus is sent to preach the kingdom of God to diverse peoples
Jesus’ mission is limited only to Israel
Jesus focuses solely on physical healing without proclamation
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is sent to preach the kingdom of God to diverse peoples
questions.explanation: Luke 4:18 highlights Jesus’ anointing to preach deliverance, and Luke 4:43 states He must preach to other cities, together teaching that Jesus’ mission extends beyond Israel to proclaim God's kingdom universally.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Luke 4:33–36 exaggerates Jesus’ authority over demons. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Jesus exercises divine authority commanding unclean spirits to obey
Demons have more power than Jesus
Jesus is powerless against spiritual forces
The exorcisms are metaphorical, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus exercises divine authority commanding unclean spirits to obey
questions.explanation: Luke 4:33–36 shows Jesus commanding an unclean spirit to come out of a man, demonstrating His divine authority over demonic powers, affirming His deity and messianic role.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s providential protection is taught in Luke 4:10–11 during Jesus' temptation?
options: God commands His angels to guard and protect His Son
God allows His Son to be harmed without intervention
Protection is unnecessary for the Messiah
Angels have no role in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God commands His angels to guard and protect His Son
questions.explanation: Luke 4:10–11 quotes Psalm 91 to show that God orders His angels to bear Jesus up and protect Him, teaching the doctrine of divine providence and angelic ministry in safeguarding God's purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially illustrated in Luke 4:41 when Jesus silences demons who confess Him as Christ?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: In Luke 4:41, Jesus rebukes demons who know His identity but forbids them to speak, reflecting His holiness and separation from evil, asserting His moral purity and divine authority.

questions.question: What theological implication about salvation and inclusion is drawn from Luke 4:25–27?
options: God’s salvation extends to Gentiles and outsiders, not only Israel
God’s miracles are confined to the Jewish elite
Salvation is limited to the physically healthy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s salvation extends to Gentiles and outsiders, not only Israel
questions.explanation: Luke 4:25–27 cites Elijah and Elisha helping Gentile widows and Naaman the Syrian, teaching that God's saving grace and miracles reach beyond Israel to include outsiders.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 4:15 and Luke 4:32 teach regarding the nature of Jesus' teaching ministry?
options: Jesus teaches with authority and is glorified by the people
Jesus’ teaching is ignored and ineffective
Jesus only teaches in private settings
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus teaches with authority and is glorified by the people
questions.explanation: Luke 4:15 describes Jesus being glorified, and Luke 4:32 notes His teaching was with power, together teaching that Jesus' ministry was marked by authoritative teaching and public acclaim.
